feedback: Iteration 0 has no earlier race results and no raced candidate, so this review rests only on the contract and the candidate's own contents. I checked it against the contract: five sensors match five weights, all sensor x-positions are within ±0.08 m, y = 0.03 m is within range, sensor_size 0.012 m is allowed, and every controller field is inside its limit. The candidate is valid and not obviously broken, so it is worth racing for telemetry. Its rationale claims an average speed near 1.5 m/s and completion within 3 s, but nothing has measured that yet, so treat it as a hypothesis. The off-track arithmetic in the rationale is right: the limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.03) = 0.06 m. Once this race reports, use the telemetry as follows. If steering_oscillation is high, or max_error is large on the slalom, lower kp (try 2.0) and raise kd (try 0.1 to 0.2). If completion is 0 with progress below about 0.9 and completion_time is near 3 s, raise base_speed (try 1.8 to 2.0) and only then consider kp. If line_loss_events is above 0 on any track, add a sixth sensor at x = ±0.03 and widen the span, or switch line_loss to search_left or search_right depending on which side the line is lost. If rms_error is high but oscillation is low, raise kp slightly (3.5 to 4.0) before changing speed. Change one group of fields per revision so the effect stays readable.
requested_changes: After the race, if steering_oscillation is high or max_error is large, set controller.kp to 2.0 and controller.kd to 0.15, keeping sensor_weights unchanged (the baseline race result should show which).
If completion is 0 with progress below 0.9 and completion_time is near 3 s, set controller.base_speed to 1.9 while keeping kp and kd from the baseline.
If line_loss_events is above 0, add a sensor at x = ±0.03, y = 0.03 with a matching weight of ±0.75 to widen the span, and test line_loss = last_direction against search_left.
